subject.title: fix(cron): keep system event queued when main-session heartbeat is disabled

question: Should cron-owned main-session systemEvent wakes bypass per-agent heartbeat scheduler omission when global heartbeats are enabled?
rationale: The source fix is bounded, but it changes the meaning of explicit per-agent heartbeat configuration for cron-triggered wakes and needs maintainer intent before merge.

options.title: Accept cron-owned wake override after proof
options.body: Require redacted real cron-run proof, then accept cron scheduling as the owner of these wakes while preserving global heartbeat disable for all sources.

options.title: Keep per-agent omission authoritative
options.body: If omitting an agent from heartbeat config must suppress cron wakes too, pause this PR and keep the linked issue open for a different fix shape.

options.title: Accept source/test evidence only
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly own the compatibility change without more contributor proof, but that bypasses the normal external-PR real-behavior proof gate.

recommendation.title: Accept cron-owned wake override after proof
recommendation.body: Require redacted real cron-run proof, then accept cron scheduling as the owner of these wakes while preserving global heartbeat disable for all sources.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest recent cross-boundary signal across heartbeat summary/gate behavior and adjacent cron systemEvent delivery work.
